body.statement:
Under \(h_n=n^{-a_h}\), \(L_n=a_h\log n\), and \(s\geq8\), define
\[
 q_{2,n}=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{13/2}}}+h_n^{s-9/4},\qquad
 q_{1,n}=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{9/2}}}+h_n^{s-5/4},\qquad
 q_{0,n}=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{5/2}}}+h_n^{s-1/4}.
\]
Then
\[
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\,h_n^{s-2}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
 q_{2,n}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\,q_{1,n}q_{0,n}\longrightarrow0
\]
hold simultaneously exactly when
\[
 \frac{1}{2(s-2)}\leq a_h<\frac17.
\]
In this window, \(n h_n^7/\log n\to\infty\), \(n h_n^{13/2}/\log n\to\infty\), and \(n h_n^2L_n^2\to\infty\).
body.proof_tex:
The first limit is
\[
 \frac{n^{1/2-a_h(s-2)}}{\sqrt{a_h\log n}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
It holds if and only if \(a_h\geq1/[2(s-2)]\); equality is allowed because of the factor \((\log n)^{-1/2}\).  The stochastic part of \(q_{2,n}\) tends to zero if and only if \(n h_n^{13/2}/\log n\to\infty\), equivalently \(a_h<2/13\), and its bias part tends to zero for every \(a_h>0\).

Expand the mixed product.  Its stochastic--stochastic term, after critical normalization, is
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{9/2}}}
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{5/2}}}
 =\frac{\log n}{\sqrt{nL_n}\,h_n^{7/2}}.
\]
Since \(L_n=a_h\log n\), this tends to zero if and only if
\[
 \frac{n h_n^7}{\log n}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
which is equivalent to \(a_h<1/7\).  The two stochastic--bias terms are each bounded, up to a fixed factor, by
\[
 h_n^{s-5/2}\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{L_n}},
\]
and hence vanish for \(s\geq8\).  The bias--bias term is
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}h_n^{2s-3/2},
\]
which vanishes when \(a_h\geq1/[2(s-2)]\), because
\(a_h(2s-3/2)>1/2\).  Thus the mixed condition is equivalent to \(a_h<1/7\).  This upper bound implies \(a_h<2/13\), so it also implies \(q_{2,n}\to0\).  Finally, \(a_h<1/7<1/2\) gives \(n h_n^2L_n^2\to\infty\).  Combining the necessary lower and upper inequalities proves the claim.
body.justification: The mixed high-times-low expansion exposes the sharp polynomial window used by the inference descendants.
body.gap: It replaces the earlier squared-high-norm arithmetic, whose upper endpoint was unnecessarily restrictive.
body.consumer: Used by lem:uniform-critical-estimates, thm:joint-critical-clt, and thm:matched-critical-risk.
